get_concept.description: Read everything Thot publishes about one concept: its name in English, French and German, the other names it goes by, where it sits among the broader and narrower terms, the XML value attached to it, and (for a concept in the date thesaurus) the range it covers, both as Thot writes it and as numbers you can sort on. This is the one step behind a catalogue record that stores nothing but 'thot-374' and has to show a king's name and his dates.

get_thesaurus.description: Read a whole Thot thesaurus: every term in it, in the language you choose. The API serves a thesaurus as the nested source of a tree widget; this brings it back as rows, each carrying its identifier, the term above it, how deep it sits and the whole path down to it, so a workflow can filter and join it without walking a tree.

search_thesaurus.description: Find the concepts in a thesaurus whose term matches some text, closest match first. Every other step here needs a 'thot-' identifier and nothing in Thot turns a word into one, so this is where a workflow starts from a term someone typed. Case and accents are ignored, and each match comes back with the whole path down to it so a term that appears twice can be told apart.

description: Look up the Egyptological vocabulary published by Thot (Thesauri & Ontology for documenting Ancient Egyptian Resources), the University of Liège project whose thesauri give projects working on ancient Egyptian texts and monuments a shared set of terms for scripts, languages, genres, object types and dates. Turn a 'thot-' identifier into a term in English, French or German, read a reign's date range as text and as numbers you can sort on, pull a whole thesaurus back as rows, search one for the term someone typed, or take a concept's SKOS record as RDF. No account or API key is required.
